title: Merida Scultura Review: The Best Road Bike For the Money?

takeaways.text: The CF3 frame (CF5 is the pro-level grade) borrows aero tube shapes and dropped seatstays from the Reacto, with hoses routed under an FSA SMR stem.

It is not light to lift but rides fast and sprightly; comfort on 28 mm GP5000s at about 60 psi is in the same class as a Tarmac or Giant TCR, though the S-Flex seatpost does less than Canyon's split post.
Clearance is 30 mm; the long, low race geometry steers quickly but predictably at slow speeds.
Dislikes: the under-saddle multitool blocks a saddle bag, the chunky FSA stem limits stack reduction, and the carbon wheels are only 19 mm wide internally.

disclosure: How the test bike was supplied is not stated. The Scultura 7000 tested uses the same CF3 frame as the candidate's 6000 but a SRAM Rival AXS build with carbon wheels.
summary: A ride review of the fifth-generation Merida Scultura 7000 on the CF3 frame shared with the Scultura 6000.
